extracted.intended_audience: prospective Helen Hay Whitney Foundation research fellowship applicants; early-career biomedical researchers; institutional administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and program description for applicants to the Helen Hay Whitney Foundation three-year research fellowship, an early-career award supporting basic biomedical scientists and requiring participation in an annual fellows' meeting where progress is reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — early-career researchers planning biomedical careers
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants financial support to young men and women planning careers in biological or medical research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program is aimed at early-career individuals who intend to pursue research careers in biology or medicine; the Foundation’s goal is to increase the number of imaginative, well-trained, and dedicated medical scientists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field of research — basic biomedical sciences
rubrics_metrics.description: Originally focused on rheumatic fever and rheumatic heart disease and later diseases of connective tissue, the Foundation ultimately expanded its interests to include all basic biomedical sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants' research should fall within the domain of basic biomedical science (broadly interpreted based on the Foundation’s historical expansion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship duration and scale — three-year support; cohort size
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation grants financial support of a three-year duration to recipients; approximately 24 three-year research fellowships are awarded annually (resulting in a total of 72 outstanding fellowships in a rolling cohort).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowships are multi-year (three years) commitments by the Foundation; applicants should plan projects and career plans consistent with a three-year fellowship period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection emphasis — imaginative, well-trained, dedicated candidates
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation’s ultimate goal is increasing the number of imaginative, well-trained, and dedicated medical scientists; fellowship recipients are expected to embody these qualities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection and support prioritize candidates who demonstrate creativity, strong training/preparation, and commitment to a career in scientific research; alumni track record indicates fellows often become highly regarded professionals and mentors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual fellows' meeting — presentation, evaluation, and interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: An annual 2–3 day meeting is held for fellows, scientific advisors, selected outside scientists and trustees to provide a forum for semiformal presentation of ongoing and proposed research and to allow evaluation by the Scientific Advisory Committee (SAC) of fellows' progress and potential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows are expected to present their research at this meeting; the SAC uses these presentations to assess progress and future potential. The meeting is designed to encourage free interactions among participants and is held in a secluded, attractive location with expenses paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program aim — long-term development of career scientists and mentors
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation regards its most critical investment as development of career scientists who will contribute by both conducting research and training future generations of scientists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and fellows are implicitly evaluated on potential for long-term contribution to the scientific enterprise, including future mentoring and leadership roles in research and training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program history and outcomes — expectation of excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: Since its inception the Foundation has awarded over 1,400 research fellowships and Whitney Fellows have gone on to become some of the most highly regarded medical and scientific professionals in their fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This historical outcome signals the Foundation’s expectation that fellows will achieve high levels of professional success; applicants should present trajectories and accomplishments consistent with that expectation.
